summary.one_liner: DemoGPT is an open-source Python project that generates LangChain code and Streamlit apps from natural-language instructions, and also ships the DemoGPT AgentHub library for building tool-using LLM agents with RAG and vector stores.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes two parts. The original DemoGPT pipeline takes a user instruction, generates a plan, creates tasks, writes code snippets, and assembles them into an interactive Streamlit app; it can be run from the command line via the demogpt package or as a Python library. The DemoGPT AgentHub library provides a BaseTool class for custom tools, built-in tools (such as TavilySearchTool, WeatherTool, WikipediaTool, PythonTool, ArxivTool, YoutubeSearchTool, PubmedTool, and YoloTool for object detection), and agent classes ToolCallingAgent and ReactAgent. It also offers BaseRAG for retrieval-augmented generation over PDF, TXT, CSV, and JSON files, with vector store options named as chroma, pinecone, and faiss. Example outputs show agents combining RAG, web search, and Python calculation to answer multi-step questions. The README lists a planned Gorilla integration for external API calls, and a to-do list with several unchecked items.
use_cases: generate a Streamlit app from a plain-English description
build an LLM agent that uses web search and a weather tool
add retrieval-augmented question answering over my documents
answer questions over a PDF resume or text files
create custom tools for an LLM agent
run object detection on an image through an agent
how_to_run: pip install .  (from a cloned repo, source code version)
notable: Turns a natural-language instruction into LangChain code and a runnable Streamlit app through a staged plan-task-snippet-assembly pipeline
AgentHub lets you create custom tools by subclassing BaseTool with a name, description, and run method
BaseRAG wraps document ingestion and querying across multiple vector stores
Example outputs show the agent's reasoning, tool calls, and decisions in verbose mode
caveats: Several to-do items are unchecked, including self-refining, Gorilla API integration, and Llama2 support
README says the code generation pipeline uses GPT-3.5-turbo by default and that API usage via Gorilla is planned, not yet available
Example outputs show an OpenAI model and external API keys are implied but setup details for keys are only partly covered
